hints: Focus on the 3D shape of each molecule, as only flat shapes like linear, trigonal planar and bent can have all atoms in one plane.
Remember that pyramidal molecules like $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{PH}_3$ have an atom sticking out of the plane, so any set containing them cannot work.
Check the tricky $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ carefully, as propene and cyclopropane both have hydrogens sticking above and below the carbon plane, then look for the set where all three are flat.
walkthrough:
**What does planar really mean?**

All atoms in the molecule must be able to sit flat on the same piece of paper. Linear, bent (with 3 atoms) and trigonal planar shapes can do this.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{linear, bent (3 atoms), trigonal planar} \rightarrow \text{planar}$$

**Spot the non-planar shapes**

Pyramidal molecules have 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair, so one atom sticks up like a pyramid top. Both $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{PH}_3$ are trigonal pyramidal and are not planar.

**Check the familiar planar molecules**

$\text{BF}_3$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$ (as single molecules) are trigonal planar with bond angle $120^{\circ}$, so they are planar. $\text{CO}_2$ is linear $\text{O=C=O}$, so it is planar. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is bent but with only 3 atoms, any 3 atoms always define one plane, so it is planar. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (ethene) has $\text{C=C}$ with all 6 atoms in one plane.

**Test the $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ trap**

$\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ is either propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$, or cyclopropane. In propene the $\text{CH}_3$ hydrogens stick out of the plane, and in cyclopropane the $\text{CH}_2$ hydrogens stick above and below the ring. So $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ is not planar.

**Pick the all-planar set**

Only the set with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has three planar molecules with no pyramidal or non-planar member.

options.A: $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{BF}_3$ are trigonal planar and are planar, but $\text{PH}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal like $\text{NH}_3$ with a lone pair pushing the P out of the plane. One non-planar member means the set fails.
options.B: $\text{AlCl}_3$ is trigonal planar and $\text{CO}_2$ is linear, both planar, but $\text{NH}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal and not planar. Students often confuse pyramidal with planar because the base looks flat, but the N atom sits above it.
options.C: $\text{BF}_3$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ are planar, but $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ is not. Whether propene or cyclopropane, some H atoms lie above and below the carbon plane, so not all atoms are in one plane.
options.D: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ is planar around the $\text{C=C}$ bond, $\text{CO}_2$ is linear so all 3 atoms are in a line and hence in a plane, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is bent but 3 atoms always lie in one plane. All three satisfy the condition.
